## Says

- "Come back at lamplighting, dearie. That's when the stories start."
- "On Monday it came out of the ground. On Thursday, the sky. Who's to say?"
- "Four peoples, four tales, and I've kept every one of them."
- "Hush, Simkin. I got it wrong on purpose."
- "Some stories climb the roofs before the sun is up."

??? quote "Dialogue"

    - **Winifred**, seventy-four and born in this very lane. I married the cobbler next door forty-nine years ago, and we've argued happily ever since.
    - Half the children of the old quarters grew up on my doorstep. My grandson [Hodge](../npcs/hodge.md) grew up a little higher than that.
    - As a girl I sewed for the envoys' households, and every one of the four peoples told it differently. In the Savage halls it was a horned giant wreathed in flame. The others told it their own ways.
    - But they all agree on the ending: the four peoples beat it once, together, and the kingdom they made is still here. That's the part I always tell twice.
    - The one I'm telling, dearie, for as long as I'm telling it. The children argue all the way home, and that's the whole point.
    - Off you go. Come back at lamplighting, and I'll tell it differently.
    - Well now, a new face on my step. Sit down, *Player*, the stool won't bite. What would you like to hear?
        - *Choice:* Who are you?
        - *Choice:* Tell me about the Balrog.
        - *Choice:* Which version is true?
        - *Choice:* Another evening.
    - Come at lamplighting, dearie. Tonight the meadow stays green at the end of the story.
